body:
### Problem

For a forced blockwise motion (`:help o_CTRL-V`), `g@` sets `']` to an incorrect position. Vim sets the correct position.

Example: `g@<C-v>j` with the cursor on `a`:

```
seed
ab
cd
```

The block is `a` and `c` .

| mark | expected (Vim) | Nvim      |
|------|----------------|-----------|
| `'[` | 2:1 (`a`)      | 2:1 (`a`) |
| `']` | 3:1 (`c`)      | 2:2 (`b`) |

`g@<C-v>e` from the same position makes a different block, `ab`, but gives the same marks. Thus the opfunc cannot know the block.

Nvim has two errors:

1. Nvim moves `']` back one character. Here `']` is on column 1, so it goes to the end of the line above.
2. On a short last line, `']` loses the right edge of the block. In the 3rd case of the repro, the block is columns 2-4, but the last line is `ab`. With `virtualedit=block`, Vim gives `'] = [3, 3, 1]` (column 3 plus `coladd` 1 = column 4). The `CountSpaces` example in `:help g@` uses this. Nvim gives `[3, 2, 0]`.

Built-in operators are correct: `y<C-v>j` yanks the correct block.

Before #42119, an opfunc could read the block from `'<`/`'>`. #42119 (correctly) stops this. Now an opfunc has no correct source for the block. I found this in a plugin: on nightly, `g@<C-v>j` changed the previous Visual selection of the user (Nagato-Yuzuru/bang.nvim#69).

Possible cause: Vim keeps a block in a separate `oap->block_mode`. For `j`, `motion_type` stays `MLINE`, so `do_pending_operator()` sets `oap->inclusive = TRUE`. In Nvim, `get_op_vcol()` sets `motion_type = kMTBlockWise` before this check (since 6cc15ccc3b, v0.1.5). Thus `inclusive` stays false, and `op_function()` applies `decl()` to `']`.



### Steps to reproduce

`nvim --clean -S repro.vim`, with `repro.vim`:

```vim
func! Op(type) abort
  let g:marks = [getpos("'[")[1:3], getpos("']")[1:3]]
endfunc
set operatorfunc=Op
func! Show(lines, keys) abort
  %delete _
  call setline(1, a:lines)
  exe "normal! " . a:keys
  let r = g:marks
  exe "normal! " . substitute(a:keys, 'g@', 'y', '')
  return printf("%-14s '[ %s  '] %s   y: %s", strtrans(a:keys), r[0], r[1], getreg('"', 1, 1))
endfunc
let out = []
call add(out, Show(['seed', 'ab', 'cd'], "2G0g@\<C-v>j"))
call add(out, Show(['seed', 'ab', 'cd'], "2G0g@\<C-v>e"))
set virtualedit=block
call add(out, Show(['abcdef', 'abcdef', 'ab'], "1G4|g@\<C-v>2j"))
set virtualedit=
call add(out, Show(['abcd'], "1G2|g@\<C-v>l"))
echo join(out, "\n")
```

Each line shows the keys, `'[` and `']` as `[line, col, coladd]`, and the text that `y` yanks with the same motion.

Nvim (0.12.5 and nightly):

```
2G0g@^Vj       '[ [2, 1, 0]  '] [2, 2, 0]   y: ['a', 'c']
2G0g@^Ve       '[ [2, 1, 0]  '] [2, 2, 0]   y: ['ab']
1G4|g@^V2j     '[ [1, 2, 0]  '] [3, 2, 0]   y: ['bcd', 'bcd', 'b ']
1G2|g@^Vl      '[ [1, 2, 0]  '] [1, 2, 0]   y: ['bc']
```


### Expected behavior

`']` gives the last line and the right edge of the block, as in Vim (`vim -u DEFAULTS -S repro.vim`):

```
2G0g@^Vj       '[ [2, 1, 0]  '] [3, 1, 0]   y: ['a', 'c']
2G0g@^Ve       '[ [2, 1, 0]  '] [2, 2, 0]   y: ['ab']
1G4|g@^V2j     '[ [1, 2, 0]  '] [3, 3, 1]   y: ['bcd', 'bcd', 'b  ']
1G2|g@^Vl      '[ [1, 2, 0]  '] [1, 2, 0]   y: ['bc']
```

The last line (`<C-v>l`, an exclusive charwise motion) is also incorrect in Vim: `y` yanks 2 columns, but `']` gives 1 column. Possibly one fix corrects all cases: `op_function()` does not apply `decl()` to a blockwise `']`. I can send a PR for the fix that you prefer.


### Nvim version (nvim -v)

v0.13.0-dev-1828+g7e1ae5115f (also v0.12.5)

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

No for linewise motions (`<C-v>j`): Vim 9.1.1752 sets the correct `']`. Yes for exclusive charwise motions (`<C-v>l`).

### Operating system/version

macOS 15.6

### Terminal name/version

n/a (reproduced with `--headless`)

### $TERM environment variable

n/a

### Installation

nightly release tarball; Homebrew for 0.12.5

comment_data.body:
The same `']` error also occurs with the built-in `y`, without 'operatorfunc': nvim --clean ``` :call setline(1, ['abcd', 'abcd']) gg0yj `] ``` `y` yanks the correct block (`a`, `a`). But `` `] `` moves the cursor to 1:4 (the end of line 1). In Vim 9.1.1752, it moves to 2:1. Same result in Nvim 0.12.5 and nightly. The `CountSpaces` example in `:help g@` also gives incorrect results for a forced blockwise motion. `:help g@` says "The type can be forced", and the example has code for blocks. `nvim --clean -S cs.vim`. `cs.vim` is the example from `:help g@`, and then these lines: ```vim call setline(1, ['a', ' ']) exe "normal 1G1|\\j" call setline(1, ['x ', 'x ', 'x']) exe "normal 1G2|\\2j" call setline(1, ['a b', '', '']) exe "normal 1G2|\\l" ``` | Keys | Block | Spaces | Vim 9.1.1752 | Nvim 0.12.5 and nightly | |---|---|---|---|---| | `j` | `a`, ` ` | 1 | 1 | 0 | | `2j` | column 2 of lines 1-3 | 2 | 2 | 0 | | `l` | columns 2-3 of line 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | Rows 1 and 2 have the same `']` error as above. Row 3 is the exclusive charwise case: Vim has the same error.
CountSpaces, from :help g@ ```vim nnoremap CountSpaces() xnoremap CountSpaces() " doubling works on a line nnoremap CountSpaces() .. '_' function CountSpaces(context = {}, type = '') abort if a:type == '' let context = #{ \ dot_command: v:false, \ extend_block: '', \ virtualedit: [&l:virtualedit, &g:virtualedit], \ } let &operatorfunc = function('CountSpaces', [context]) set virtualedit=block return 'g@' endif let save = #{ \ clipboard: &clipboard, \ selection: &selection, \ virtualedit: [&l:virtualedit, &g:virtualedit], \ register: getreginfo('"'), \ visual_marks: [getpos("'<"), getpos("'>")], \ } try set clipboard= selection=inclusive virtualedit= let commands = #{ \ line: "'[V']", \ char: "`[v`]", \ block: "`[\`]", \ }[a:type] let [_, _, col, off] = getpos("']") if off != 0 let vcol = getline("'[")->strpart(0, col + off)->strdisplaywidth() if vcol >= [line("'["), '$']->virtcol() - 1 let a:context.extend_block = '$' else let a:context.extend_block = vcol .. '|' endif endif if a:context.extend_block != '' let commands ..= 'oO' .. a:context.extend_block endif let commands ..= 'y' execute 'silent noautocmd keepjumps normal! ' .. commands echomsg getreg('"')->count(' ') finally call setreg('"', save.register) call setpos("'<", save.visual_marks[0]) call setpos("'>", save.visual_marks[1]) let &clipboard = save.clipboard let &selection = save.selection let [&l:virtualedit, &g:virtualedit] = get(a:context.dot_command ? save : a:context, 'virtualedit') let a:context.dot_command = v:true endtry endfunction ```
@ShiAnPoQing Not the same issue, I think. This one is '] off by one for a non-empty block, while #42298 is about empty charwise motions (#19426).

title: 'operatorfunc' cannot get the block of a forced blockwise motion (`g@<C-v>j`)
